guarantees.claim: When hash_start_sha_disabled is true, err_code is driven to SwHashStartWhenShaDisabled, regardless of other inputs.
When hash_start_sha_disabled is false and hash_start_active is true, err_code is driven to SwHashStartWhenActive.
When both hash_start_sha_disabled and hash_start_active are false and msg_push_not_allowed is true, err_code is driven to SwPushMsgWhenDisallowed.
When all previous conditions are false and update_seckey_inprocess is true, err_code is driven to SwUpdateSecretKeyInProcess.
When none of the listed error conditions are true, err_code is driven to NoError.

uncertain_points.claim: Duplicate condition hash_start_sha_disabled on line 856 makes the second branch unreachable, likely a copy-paste error that may have omitted a different intended condition.
uncertain_points.risk: If a real error condition was intended but is missing due to the duplicate, that error will go undetected, potentially compromising security or functional integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: Priority order places update_seckey_inprocess (secret-key related) at the lowest priority; if it co-occurs with higher-priority errors like msg_push_not_allowed, the secret-key condition is hidden.
uncertain_points.risk: A critical security-related error may be masked, delaying or preventing proper error handling.
